q-52309.name: Question 1
q-52309.worked_solution:
We write the term under the radical as a perfect cube, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{{a}^{6}{b}^{6}} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{{a}^{2}{b}^{2}\cdot {a}^{2}{b}^{2}\cdot {a}^{2}{b}^{2}} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{{({a}^{2}{b}^{2})}^{3}} & = \\ {a}^{2}{b}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-82153.name: Question 3
q-82153.worked_solution:
To simplify the expression, we write the term under the radical as a perfect cube, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{125(x+8y)^{3}} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{5(x+8y)\cdot 5(x+8y)\cdot 5(x+8y)} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{{(5(x+8y))}^{3}} & = \\ 5(x+8y)\end{aligned}
$$

q-82153.html:
Question 3
?

Simplify 125(x+8y)33.

a
125(x+8y)
b
5(x3+2y3)
c
25(x+2y)
d
5(x+8y)
e
5x+8y3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To simplify the expression, we write the term under the radical as a perfect cube, and simplify:

125(x+8y)33=5(x+8y)⋅5(x+8y)⋅5(x+8y)3=(5(x+8y))33=5(x+8y)
q-82153.knowledge_point: Finding Cube Roots of Terms Containing Binomials

a
8x−13
b
2x3−1
c
8x
d
2x−1

2x
Submit

q-82158.name: Question 5
q-82158.worked_solution:
To simplify the expression, we write the term under the radical as a perfect cube, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{\frac{{x}^{6}}{{p}^{6}}} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{p}^{2}})\cdot (\frac{{x}^{2}}{{p}^{2}})\cdot (\frac{{x}^{2}}{{p}^{2}})} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{p}^{2}})}^{3}} & = \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{p}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

x3p3

xp2
c
xp
d
x3p
e
x2p2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To simplify the expression, we write the term under the radical as a perfect cube, and simplify:

q-82155.name: Question 6
q-82155.worked_solution:
To simplify the expression, we write the term under the radical as a perfect cube, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{\frac{125}{(3-x)^{3}}} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{\frac{5}{(3-x)}\cdot \frac{5}{(3-x)}\cdot \frac{5}{(3-x)}} & = \\ \sqrt[3]{{(\frac{5}{(3-x)})}^{3}} & = \\ \frac{5}{(3-x)}\end{aligned}
$$

?

125(3−x)33=

a
25(3−x)2
b
25(3−x)
c
5(3−x)
d
5(3−x)2
e
10(3−x)
